messages.author: 23a2cb256755f4e1
messages.subject: DMR are found meanly at poorly coverd regions
parts:
In a previous post "Outfiles listing diferentially methylated sites are empty" I found out that searching for  differentially methylated regions (DMR) and for differentially methylated cytosines (DMC) can produce NOT CORRESPONDING RESULTS. In my case this was drastic because I found 1000 DMR but ZERO  DMC. I'm still thinking I'm doing something wrong with the sequence of commands or the argunments I'm using. I will appreciate further help with this issue.
Following the discussion and advise provided by Altuna I found out that most of my DMR are called in regions of the genome with very low coverage ( less than 5 reads per cytosine). However I think that I have a decent coverage.

At first I would like to find differentially methylated cytosines (since  I'm doing methyl seq to have single base resolution).

###After reading my files I create an "myobj" containing them.
### I first filtered by a coverage.

> filtered.myobj=filterByCoverage(myobj,lo.count=8,lo.perc=NULL,hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)

#### Then I will merge samples , but HERE I HAVE A QUESTION

### IT IS THIS?

> meth=unite(myobj, destrand = FALSE)

#### or rather is this?

> meth=unite (filtered.myobj, destrand = FALSE)


#### also here I have another doubt. I will like to use destrand = TRUE, when focusing in CG methylation. But what happens is that after filtering information for many CG remain in only one strand.
#### CAN I FIRST CREATE A methylBase object and then filter element of this object in term of coverage?

#### hope that someone can help me with this.

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] DMR are found meanly at poorly coverd regions
parts: Following the discussion and advise provided by Altuna I found out that most of my DMR are called in regions of the genome with very low coverage ( less than 5 reads per cytosine). However I think that I have a decent coverage.
In my opinion, you should remove everything below 10X before you do any analysis.

At first I would like to find differentially methylated cytosines (since  I'm doing methyl seq to have single base resolution).

###After reading my files I create an "myobj" containing them.
### I first filtered by a coverage.

> filtered.myobj=filterByCoverage(myobj,lo.count=8,lo.perc=NULL,hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)

#### Then I will merge samples , but HERE I HAVE A QUESTION

### IT IS THIS?

> meth=unite(myobj, destrand = FALSE)

#### or rather is this?

> meth=unite (filtered.myobj, destrand = FALSE)
the second option is what you want to do here, I think: meth=unite (filtered.myobj, destrand = FALSE)
#### also here I have another doubt. I will like to use destrand = TRUE, when focusing in CG methylation. But what happens is that after filtering information for many CG remain in only one strand.

CG methylation is mostly symmetric (in many human samples I looked at). If that's the case for your species, it doesn't matter if filtering removes coverage on one strand mostly. You can still treat them equally and pool them.
#### CAN I FIRST CREATE A methylBase object and then filter element of this object in term of coverage?

Yes you can do this, but not with the  filterByCoverage() function but using the [] notation.
You should be able to subset methylBase object the way you would subset the rows of a data.frame.

assume "mbase" is a methylBase object. The code below will create a new methylBase object where
the coverage values from the 1st and 2nd sample above 10.

mbase[mbase$coverage1>10 & mbase$coverage2>10, ]


Best,
Altuna

Yes you write it is symmetric, but still I do not complete understand how methylKit handle it.  

Lets say that I filter and then compare: and I have this situation

chr    start     end   strand  coverage    #C     #T                      chr     start       end     strand     coverage    #C      #T

chr1  1001   1001   -           4               0      3                          chr1   1001    1001      -               8              1         7

If I first I filter by coverage (cutoff = or >10), then unite  and then compare meth, I will have not data in this particular CG. But if I first unite, then filter by coverage and finally compare I will be able to include this particular CG in my comparison. I'm write?

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] DMR are found meanly at poorly coverd regions
parts:
Hi Alejandro,
Yes, that is correct. In your example, the CpG will be filtered out if you apply the coverage cut-off 10X before unite(). But if you don't apply the cutoff, do unite( destrand=TRUE) and then filter using the [] notation then, your example CpG will be in your set. 

Best,
Altuna
